from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Geometry of Cycles", [
            "Euler's formula describes rotation via complex numbers.",
            "We represent this as a phasor tracing a circle.",
            "Rotation in the complex plane creates a cycle."
        ])
        
        # Complex plane coordinate system
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "include_tip": True}
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        point = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        phasor = Line(start=circle.get_center(), end=circle.get_start(), color="#00FFFF")
        
        # Trackers
        angle = ValueTracker(0)
        phasor.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(
            circle.get_center(),
            circle.get_center() + np.array([np.cos(angle.get_value()), np.sin(angle.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(phasor.get_end()))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.add(phasor, point)
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fourier series build shapes from epicycles.",
            "Circles added together form complex periodic paths.",
            "Radii and frequencies determine the path's shape.",
            "This synthesis constructs any periodic function.",
            "See how these vectors trace the cat's path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Epicycles: The Fourier Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize shapes
        c1 = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#FFFFFF")
        c2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFFF00")
        
        v1 = Vector(RIGHT, color="#FFFFFF")
        v2 = Vector(RIGHT, color="#FFFF00")
        
        # Positioning at grid
        self.place_at_grid(c1, "B2")
        c2.next_to(c1.get_right(), RIGHT, buff=0)
        
        # Trackers
        angle1 = ValueTracker(0)
        angle2 = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Path tracer
        path = TracedPath(c2.get_right, stroke_color="#FF0000", stroke_width=2)
        
        self.add(c1, c2, v1, v2, path)
        
        # Udpater to keep circles linked
        c2.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(c1.get_right() + [0.5, 0, 0]))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        # Animation rotation
        c1.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 0.5, about_point=c1.get_center()))
        c2.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.rotate(dt * 2.0, about_point=c2.get_center()))
        self.wait(4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Connecting to the Heat Equation", [

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Circular frequencies dictate heat dissipation rates.",
            "Fourier modes describe a ring's cooling.",
            "Temperature evolves through its circular components."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Overlay the epicycle path on a complex plane grid.
        axes = ComplexPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2]).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(axes))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show final transformation from epicycles to a wave.
        circle = Circle(radius=1, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'F3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(wave))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the final combined resulting function clearly.
        final_func = MathTex(r"T(\theta, t) = \sum a_n e^{in\theta} e^{-\lambda_n t}", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(final_func, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(final_func))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: From Circles to Heat: The Magic of Fourier Series

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Cycles
sections.content: Briefly recap Euler's formula (e^iθ = cosθ + isinθ) to establish how complex numbers represent rotation. Visualize this as a point tracing a circle.
sections.example: An animation showing a single rotating vector (phasor) tracing a perfect circle on the complex plane.

sections.title: Epicycles: The Fourier Synthesis
sections.content: Introduce the concept of Fourier Series as 'epicycles.' Explain that any periodic function can be reconstructed by adding together multiple circles of different frequencies and radii.
sections.example: An animation of 'Fourier the Cat': several circles linked together where the tip of the final vector traces the outline of a cat’s head.

sections.title: Connecting to the Heat Equation
sections.content: Transition to the Heat Equation (∂u/∂t = α∇²u). Explain that heat flow is a 'smoothing' process. Fourier series act as the building blocks (eigenfunctions) that describe how a temperature distribution evolves over time.
sections.example: Visualizing a metal rod. An initial 'jagged' temperature profile is decomposed into simple sine waves; watch how high-frequency waves (sharp details) decay faster than low-frequency waves.

sections.title: Synthesis & Application
sections.content: Connect the circular representation back to the heat equation: the 'frequencies' of the circles determine how fast different parts of the heat distribution dissipate.
sections.example: A 'Heat-Map Clock' where the temperature of a circular ring changes over time; the Fourier components represent the cooling modes of the ring.
